title.narrative: Enhanced institutionalisation of human rights-based data collection on HRE/SDG 4.7 and strengthened national implementation of its HRE elements in two African countries
NHRIs in Africa are collaborating with relevant state actors to further the institutionalisation of human rights-based data collection on SDG 4.7 and progress in human rights education.

target.value: 2 NHRIs in two different African countries in Eastern or Southern Africa are working with relevant state actors on the institutionalisation of data collection for SDG and human rights monitoring processes and using the human rights data to further progress at the national level on implementation of HRE/SDG 4.7.

actual.value: 3 NHRIs are collaborating with a range of relevant national actors to further HRE in national frameworks. However, it has not been possible within the short time-frame of the small grants to secure the institutionalization of human rights-based data collection, although one NHRI, the Ethiopian Human Rights Commission, has included in their recently developed Action Plan that they will produce annual reports on the HRE elements of SDG 4.7.

title.narrative: Output 2.1: Technical Assistance to two NHRIs

DIHR has provided technical support to 2 NHRIs to further integrated reporting on the human rights education elements of SDG 4.7 and to strengthen the implementation of human rights education at the national level.

target.value: Based on identified needs the DIHR has provided technical support to the two selected NHRIs to further their efforts to promote human rights education within some of the following areas: Policy development,Curricula development, teacher Education, Student Assessments or promotion of a human rights-based learning environment.

actual.value: 3 NHRI in Kenya, Ethiopia and Cameroon received grants out of a pool of applications from 7 NHRIs in the region.

target.value: Project agreement and results framework has been finalised.
Engagement improved between national human rights institution and national education authorities on strengthening HRE.

actual.value: In Kenya, Ethiopia and Cameroon, NHRIs have engaged with a range of national stakeholders, including Ministries of Education, Curriculum Institutes, Teacher Training Institutes, and schools drawing on the data collected through the use of the SDG 4.7/Human Rights Education Indicators and Online Tool. In the three countries, this has led to engagements between national human rights institution and national education authorities on strengthening human rights education in education sector plans, in the official school curriculum, and in the curriculum for teacher education.

title.narrative: The Human Rights Indicator Framework is developed into an online tool linking human rights standards on human rights education to SDG 4.7 and its human rights education elements. Online tool in English is available on DIHR’s website and accessible to all.

target.value: Project agreement and results framework has been finalised.
Online tool in English available on DIHR’s website and accessible to all.

actual.value: An English version of the SDG 4.7/Human Rights Education Monitoring Tool is now online and can be accessed by all via this website https://sdg47- hre.humanrights.dk/en/node/264. The indicators and online survey have been updated based on the valuable input received from African NHRIs that have used the tool during this project period.

target.value: The methodology and guidance on how to use the tool has been finalised.

actual.value: The methodology has been finalised and discussed extensively with the OHCHR and UNESCO. Guidance in the use of the tool has been developed both on the website in the form of a manual but also in the online survey tool to facilitate responses.

title.narrative: Output 1.2: Workshop with 5 African NHRIs carried out

Regional workshop in Africa with 5 selected NHRIs from Eastern and Southern Africa to build capacity for national implementation of human rights education and SDG 4.7, based on data collected via the online tool.

target.value: Project agreement and results framework has been finalised.

Human rights data on the current implementation of the HRE elements of SDG 4.7 will be available for state actors. NHRIs. CSOs and educational institutions in five African countries through the use of DIHR’s online tool. NHRIs from the five countries have shared observations on the HRE scenarios in their respective countries based on the data generated and discussed how to take strategic follow-up action to further States implementation of HRE.

actual.value: One regional workshop was carried out online on 27 and 28 August 2020 in close co-operation with NANHRI, the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions. The workshop was attended by 24 NHRI participants from 8 NHRIs in Kenya, Ethiopia, Gambia, Ghana, Nigeria, Zimbabwe, Malawi, and Cameroon.

Two follow-up webinars on Microsoft Teams were carried out on 30 September and 28 October 2020 on Human Rights Education in National Frameworks and Deepening National Implementation of SDG 4.7 and Human Rights Education: The Learning Environment, respectively. Data on the implementation of the human rights education elements of SDG 4.7 has been submitted by 10 national human rights institutions in Kenya, Ethiopia, Zimbabwe, Sudan, Sierra Leone, Malawi, Cameroon, Nigeria, the Gambia, and Ghana.

title.narrative: Strengthened access to and capacity among selected African NHRIs to use online data tools for furthering implementation of HRE/SDG 4.7
Staff from NHRIs have documented a positive learning effect against pre-established learning and behavioural goals and NHRIs in Africa have collected data on HRE/SDG 4.7 using DIHR’s online tool.

target.value: 16 staff from 8 NHRIs have documented a positive learning effect against pre-established learning and behavioural goals.
